title: Missed Opportunities for Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Prescription in French Military Primary Care: A KAP Survey With Scenario-Based Modeling

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, yet uptake remains suboptimal. In France, routine vaccination targets early adolescence (11-14 years), with catch-up vaccination recommended up to age 26 years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional, anonymous online Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) survey was conducted in September 2025 among active-duty French Military Health Service (SSA) military general practitioners (MGPs). Responses were dichotomized as “Yes” versus “No.” Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed to identify individual factors associated with HPV vaccine prescription.
analysis.methods: The primary outcome was self-reported routine initiation of HPV vaccination via prescription.
analysis.main_results: Among approximately 800 active-duty military physicians contacted through institutional channels, 186 completed the survey and met the inclusion criteria for the present analysis, corresponding to approximately one quarter of contacted physicians. Among respondents, 70 (38%) reported routinely initiating HPV vaccination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Routine initiation of HPV vaccination via prescription appears constrained mainly by missed opportunities and organizational friction rather than clinician opposition. Scenario analyses suggested larger gains from increasing opportunities (routinized prompts/standardized encounters) and improving communication comfort than from knowledge gains alone, with additive effects when combining levers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: With expanded catch-up recommendations and extended reimbursement up to age 26 years, implementation efforts within the French armed forces are timely. Systematic prompts, streamlined prescription-to-vaccination pathways, and brief communication-focused training may increase initiation rates.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations related to the study design or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of French military general practitioners (MGPs) regarding human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination. The research aimed to understand the barriers to HPV vaccine prescription within the French Military Health Service (SSA). A cross-sectional, anonymous online KAP survey was conducted in September 2025 among approximately 800 MGPs, with 186 completing the survey. The primary outcome was self-reported routine initiation of HPV vaccination via prescription, with 70 (38%) reporting this practice. The study found that routine initiation was associated with gynecology-related clinical activity, higher HPV knowledge, and comfort in discussing sexual health. Scenario-based modeling suggested that increasing opportunities for vaccination and improving communication comfort could lead to greater initiation rates. The findings highlight the importance of addressing organizational and systemic barriers to HPV vaccination in military primary care settings.

title: Diagnostic utility of high‐risk HPV polymerase chain reaction–based testing in head and neck FNA specimens with indeterminate cytomorphology

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, but the evidence is strong due to the high positive predictive value observed in cytologically indeterminate specimens with HR-HPV positivity, which is supported by the calculated confidence interval.

The study supports integrating HR-HPV PCR into routine cytologic interpretation to upgrade some indeterminate specimens to malignant, thereby expediting treatment and reducing the need for additional invasive procedures. The findings are significant for improving diagnostic accuracy in HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancers but are limited by the retrospective design and potential for selection bias.

title: Real-World Effectiveness and Impact of Human Papillomavirus Vaccination in Males: A Comprehensive Review.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV), specifically assessing real-world vaccine effectiveness (VE) and the population-level impact of gender-neutral vaccination (GNV) in males against HPV-associated diseases such as anogenital warts (AGW), oral and penile HPV infections, and precancerous lesions or cancers. The central question focuses on the effectiveness of HPV vaccination in males and the broader public health impact of GNV programs.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a comprehensive synthesis of studies evaluating quadrivalent (4vHPV) or nonavalent (9vHPV) vaccines in males, conducted using Embase and PubMed from January 2007 to May 2024. Eligible studies assessed VE or GNV impact on HPV infections, precancerous lesions, cancer, or AGW. Risk of bias was evaluated using ROBINS-I and the National Institute of Health quality assessment tool. Twenty-one geographically diverse studies were included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Real-world evidence indicates that HPV vaccination in males substantially reduces anogenital and oral HPV infections and AGW. Vaccine effectiveness reaches up to 100% against oral HPV infection and 41% for penile HPV (4vHPV genotypes), with higher effectiveness among adolescents and those vaccinated before age 23. Among men who have sex with men, VE was 85% for penile HPV infection, 55% for AGW, and 60% for anal infection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Most studies assessing VE and vaccination impact (VI) demonstrated a risk of bias, indicating methodological limitations in the evidence base. Heterogeneity in study designs, populations, and outcomes contributes to uncertainty in pooled estimates and generalizability of findings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Priority research areas include conducting high-quality, bias-minimized studies to refine VE estimates in males, particularly for oncogenic HPV types and across diverse populations. Surveillance systems should be strengthened to monitor long-term outcomes of GNV programs, including reductions in HPV-associated cancers and infections in males. Vaccination policies should prioritize adolescent vaccination and early administration to maximize public health impact.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the real-world effectiveness of HPV vaccination in males and the population-level impact of gender-neutral vaccination (GNV) programs. Evidence from 21 geographically diverse studies indicates that HPV vaccination significantly reduces anogenital and oral HPV infections and anogenital warts in males, with higher effectiveness observed among adolescents and those vaccinated before age 23. Vaccine effectiveness reaches up to 100% against oral HPV infection and 41% for penile HPV (4vHPV genotypes), while men who have sex with men show 85% effectiveness against penile HPV infection, 55% against anogenital warts, and 60% against anal infection. However, most studies exhibit a risk of bias, highlighting methodological limitations and heterogeneity in the evidence base. The review underscores the public health significance of universal HPV vaccination programs and calls for bias-minimized research to refine estimates and strengthen surveillance of long-term outcomes.

title: Clearance of high‐risk human papillomavirus in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2–3 after the loop electrosurgical excision procedure with negative resection margins

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the longitudinal clearance rates of high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV) and the incidence of clinical recurrence in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2–3 following the loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP), addressing a gap in understanding post-treatment outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, involving 145 patients diagnosed with CIN 2–3 who underwent LEEP between January 2021 and December 2024, with an 18-month surveillance window.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed clinical records of patients diagnosed with CIN 2–3 who underwent LEEP, focusing on hr-HPV clearance rates and clinical recurrence defined by abnormal cytology or histologically confirmed CIN.
analysis.main_results: The baseline prevalence of hr-HPV was 99.3% (n = 144/145). At 6 months post-LEEP, the type-specific viral clearance rate was 74.3% (n = 107/144). At 18 months, complete hr-HPV negativity was 75.8% (47/62) among the evaluable subcohort, representing a conservative baseline minimum of 32.6% (47/144) when accounting for complete attrition bounds. The overall recurrence rate of CIN or cytological abnormalities was 11.1% (16/144), with 15 of 16 recurrences detected at the 6-month interval, of which 73.3% (11/15) demonstrated concurrent hr-HPV positivity (P = 0.0001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that LEEP facilitates significant viral clearance, but persistent hr-HPV serves as a potent biomarker for clinical recurrence, highlighting its potential role in risk stratification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of HPV-based testing at the 6-month follow-up window to optimize risk stratification and guide surveillance strategies in the context of follow-up limitations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential attrition, with a conservative estimate of 32.6% hr-HPV clearance at 18 months. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the clearance rates of high-risk human papillomavirus (hr-HPV) and the incidence of clinical recurrence in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2–3 following loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). Conducted at Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, it analyzed 145 patients between 2021 and 2024. The baseline hr-HPV prevalence was 99.3%, with 74.3% clearance at 6 months and 75.8% negativity at 18 months among the evaluable subcohort. The overall recurrence rate was 11.1%, with most recurrences detected at 6 months and concurrent hr-HPV positivity in 73.3% of these cases. The authors concluded that LEEP leads to significant viral clearance, but persistent hr-HPV is a strong biomarker for recurrence. The study's findings suggest the value of HPV-based testing at 6-month follow-ups for improved risk stratification, despite limitations such as attrition and a retrospective design.

title: Factors impacting protective immunity conferred by vaccination with adeno-associated virus-like particles displaying human papillomavirus L2 residues 17–36

analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes re-evaluating HPV42's risk classification to inform prevention and clinical management strategies. The review underscores the need for updated classification, targeted surveillance, and mechanistic research to address diagnostic and therapeutic gaps in HPV42-associated diseases.

title: [Prevalence of cervical human papillomavirus infection among women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China].

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical human papilloma virus (HPV) infection among ethnic minority and Han Chinese women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture of Yunnan Province to provide a theoretical basis for the strategy of cervical cancer prevention and treatment in this region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A consecutive cohort of 12,605 female residents who underwent cervical HPV genotyping across four medical centers in the Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture between January 2018 and June 2024 was enrolled.
analysis.methods: The overall HPV prevalence and genotype distribution was analyzed and the disparities in infection patterns among different ethnic groups were compared.
analysis.main_results: The overall HPV prevalence among women in this region was 17.88% (2,254/12,605). Infections solely with high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) predominated, with a prevalence of 14.75%, accounting for 82.48% (1,859/2,254) of all HPV-positive cases. The three most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52 (4.53%), HPV-16 (2.41%), and HPV-58 (2.01%). HPV infections exhibited a striking age-specific clustering among younger demographics; the prevalence in both the <20 and 20-29 years age groups reached 100%. The prevalence declined significantly with advancing age, dropping to 5.20% in the ≥60 years age group. Single-genotype infections constituted the primary pattern (74.00%, 1,668/2,254).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that future cervical cancer prevention and control strategies in this region should shift interventions to earlier stages, prioritizing early screening and health education for young women.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted cervical cancer prevention strategies, particularly for young women and ethnic minority populations, emphasizing the importance of early screening and health education.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and potential for selection bias, as it enrolled women who underwent cervical HPV genotyping. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and epidemiological characteristics of cervical human papillomavirus (HPV) infection among women in Honghe Hani and Yi Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China. It enrolled 12,605 female residents across four medical centers between January 2018 and June 2024. The overall HPV prevalence was 17.88%, with high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) infections predominating at 14.75%. The most common HR-HPV genotypes were HPV-52, HPV-16, and HPV-58. HPV infections showed age-specific clustering, with 100% prevalence in the <20 and 20-29 years age groups, and a significant decline in older age groups. Single-genotype infections were the primary pattern, while multiple infections were more common in younger women. Ethnic minority women had a higher prevalence of HPV compared to Han women, with the Dai, Hani, and Miao ethnicities showing the highest rates. The study suggests that cervical cancer prevention strategies should focus on early screening and health education for young women, particularly in ethnic minority communities, and highlights the need for multivalent HPV vaccines targeting the predominant strains.

title: Improving Cervical Cancer Screening Participation Through Human Papillomavirus Self-Sampling: A Scoping Review of Evidence in Underserved Populations.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human papillomaviruses (HPV) and HPV-associated cervical cancer screening in underserved populations, focusing on the acceptability and implementation of HPV self-sampling as an intervention to improve participation in cervical cancer prevention programs.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, searching PubMed and Embase for literature published between 2002 and 2025. Eligible studies reported acceptability, feasibility, or participant preferences for HPV self-sampling in marginalized populations, with data synthesized narratively. Ten studies across eight countries involving over 6400 participants were included.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HPV self-sampling achieves high acceptance rates (21% to 98%) in marginalized communities when implemented through culturally sensitive, community-engaged programs. Key facilitators include privacy, autonomy, and convenience, while barriers encompass low literacy, fear of results, and healthcare mistrust.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges methodological limitations, including restriction to two databases and reliance on narrative synthesis without pooled estimates. Evidence gaps persist regarding long-term outcomes, optimal implementation strategies across diverse settings, and the impact of self-sampling on follow-up care adherence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integrating culturally tailored education, community health worker involvement, and low-barrier follow-up care is critical to advance health equity in cervical cancer prevention. Future research should prioritize comparative effectiveness studies and implementation science to optimize self-sampling programs in underserved populations.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review evaluates HPV self-sampling as a strategy to improve cervical cancer screening participation among underserved populations. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, it synthesizes evidence from ten studies across eight countries involving over 6400 participants, highlighting high acceptance rates (21%–98%) when programs are culturally sensitive and community-engaged. Facilitators include privacy, autonomy, and convenience, while barriers such as low literacy, fear of results, and healthcare mistrust persist. Methodological limitations include reliance on two databases and narrative synthesis without pooled estimates. The review concludes that integrating education, navigation support, and accessible follow-up care can advance health equity, while calling for comparative effectiveness research and implementation science to address evidence gaps.

title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccination programmes across European countries: time-harmonized coverage among adolescent females, socioeconomic predictors, and impact on public interest

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination represents a cornerstone of cervical cancer prevention and is essential to achieving the WHO elimination targets in Europe.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This country-level longitudinal study analysed available 2010-2023 full-dose HPV vaccination coverage data among 15-year-old females across 43 European countries, by years since introduction within the National Immunization Programmes (NIPs).
analysis.methods: Socioeconomic, institutional, health-system, and delivery indicators were integrated with Google Trends Relative Search Volume for the "HPV vaccine" topic. Multivariable GEE models were used to identify predictors of vaccination coverage, while Pearson correlations assessed the association between Relative Search Volume and coverage.
analysis.main_results: Coverage among adolescent females increased markedly after NIP introduction, with population-weighted coverage reaching about 40% by year 2 and stabilising at 55-60% by year 5. Coverage exceeded 60% in most countries by year 15. Multivariable analyses identified lower public disagreement with vaccine safety and higher physician density as significant determinants, with interactions between time since NIP introduction and HDI. School-based programmes were associated with a faster increase. Among 32 countries with Google Trends data, 53% showed significant Relative Search Volume changes after NIP introduction, and Relative Search Volume strongly correlated with coverage (r = 0.89).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of socioeconomic and institutional factors in shaping HPV vaccination coverage trends and identifies public interest as a significant correlate of vaccine uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening public confidence, primary care capacity, school-based delivery, and digital monitoring could help close immunization gaps and accelerate progress toward cervical cancer elimination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on country-level data and does not account for individual-level variations, which may limit the generalisability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on observational data and correlations rather than experimental methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines HPV vaccination coverage trends among adolescent females in Europe, focusing on the impact of National Immunization Programmes (NIPs) and socioeconomic factors. It finds that coverage increased significantly after NIP introduction, reaching over 60% in most countries by year 15. Public interest, as measured by Google Trends, is strongly correlated with vaccination rates. The research identifies lower public disagreement with vaccine safety and higher physician density as key predictors of coverage, with school-based programmes associated with faster uptake. While the findings suggest potential strategies to improve vaccination rates, the study's reliance on observational data limits its generalisability. The results underscore the importance of addressing public confidence and health-system capacity to achieve cervical cancer elimination targets.

title: '...but look how many lives would have been saved if this was available then' Exploring the acceptability of future Human Papillomavirus self-sampling, and the barriers and facilitators of cervical cancer screening for those with intellectual disabilities in Scotland.

analysis.methods: Data were collected through focus groups and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis to identify key themes related to screening experiences and self-sampling acceptability.
analysis.main_results: Five main themes emerged: NHS communication as a source of distress; power imbalances between healthcare providers and women with ID; enduring consequences of inadequate care; past trauma shaping future avoidance; and self-sampling as a pathway to empowerment. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The research highlights systemic inadequacies in current cervical cancer screening services for women with ID while identifying self-sampling as a transformative potential solution. The novelty lies in centring the voices of women with ID to reveal unmet needs and propose actionable changes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Self-sampling could advance health equity goals and improve healthcare outcomes for women with ID by addressing access barriers and trauma-informed care gaps in cervical cancer screening programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The qualitative design limits generalisability, and the small sample size (n=13) may not capture the full diversity of experiences among women with ID. Evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of quantitative validation and reliance on self-reported perspectives.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explored barriers to cervical cancer screening among women with intellectual disabilities (ID) in Scotland, where screening attendance is approximately 30%, far below national and WHO targets. Using focus groups with 11 women with ID and 2 carers, researchers identified five themes: distressing NHS communication, power imbalances, enduring consequences of inadequate care, trauma-driven avoidance, and self-sampling as empowering. Participants expressed high acceptability for HPV self-sampling, viewing it as a solution to overcome traditional screening barriers. The findings reveal systemic inadequacies in current services and suggest self-sampling could improve health equity and outcomes for this underserved group. However, the small sample size and qualitative design limit generalisability, warranting further research.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem of low adolescent HPV vaccination uptake by examining why parental awareness and acceptance of HPV vaccination remain insufficient despite its proven role in preventing HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 300 parents of adolescents aged 9–18 years attending inpatient or outpatient services at Shafizadeh Children’s Hospital in Babol, Iran.
analysis.methods: Parents completed a structured questionnaire capturing demographic characteristics, awareness of HPV and HPV vaccination, attitudes toward vaccination, and perceived barriers and motivators.
analysis.main_results: Awareness of HPV infection and HPV vaccination was reported by 43.7% and 38.3% of parents, respectively, while only 14.7% correctly identified the recommended vaccination age; HPV vaccination uptake was very low, with only 4 parents (1.3%) vaccinated themselves and 2 (0.7%) having vaccinated their children.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre, cross-sectional design limits generalisability, and reliance on self-reported awareness and uptake may introduce reporting bias, warranting a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Babol, Iran assessed parental awareness, attitudes, and barriers regarding HPV infection and HPV vaccination among 300 parents of adolescents aged 9–18 years. Despite 52.7% of parents holding favorable attitudes, HPV vaccination uptake was extremely low (1.3% among parents and 0.7% among children). The authors propose integrating HPV vaccination into national programs, enhancing insurance coverage, and delivering targeted education to improve uptake.

title: Effect of thermal ablation on persistent HPV infection in Danish women ≥ 40 years of age: a quasi-randomized clinical study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection in women aged ≥40 years poses a risk for progression to cervical disease despite the absence of high-grade lesions. analysis.study_design_and_population: A quasi-randomized clinical study enrolled 131 women aged ≥40 years with persistent HR-HPV infection but without histologically confirmed high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (≥CIN2) across three outpatient gynecological clinics. After exclusions, 39 women were allocated to thermal ablation and 34 to a no-treatment control arm using quasi-randomization based on date of birth.
analysis.methods: HPV genotyping and FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation status were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 10 months. Thermal ablation was performed using the WISAP probe at 65 °C for 2 minutes and at 100 °C for 40 seconds, administered across two sessions 2–3 days apart.
analysis.main_results: At 10 months, 64.1% of women in the intervention arm and 79.4% in the control arm remained HR-HPV positive, with no significant difference between arms at any time point. FAM19A4/miR124-2 methylation positivity showed a transient decrease (-10.2%) in the intervention arm at 3 months but increased in both arms over 10 months to above baseline levels, with no significant treatment effect.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that thermal ablation does not facilitate HPV clearance or reduce oncogenic transformation risk in women with persistent HR-HPV infection without significant cervical disease, as evidenced by sustained HPV positivity and increasing methylation positivity in both arms.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s quasi-randomized design and lack of histological confirmation of high-grade lesions limit causal inference and generalizability. title: Seroprevalence of HPV Infection in Healthcare Workers with Molecular Confirmation of High-Risk HPV

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the high global burden of oncogenic human papillomaviruses (HPV), particularly HPV-16 and HPV-18, which account for over 70% of cervical cancer cases. analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among healthcare workers at Al-Shatra General Hospital and Al-Haboubi Teaching Hospital in Dhi Qar Governorate, Iraq. Participants were adults without prior HPV vaccination, no symptoms of sexually transmitted infections, and provided informed consent. Exclusions included individuals with chronic systemic diseases, pregnant women, and adults aged 60 years or older.
analysis.methods: Serum anti-HPV IgG and IgM antibodies were quantified using commercial ELISA kits. A subset of 100 seropositive samples (IgM >0.25 nmol/L) underwent conventional PCR to detect circulating cell-free DNA of HPV-16 and HPV-18. Statistical analysis used non-parametric tests due to the exploratory design and limited PCR-positive cases.
analysis.main_results: Seroprevalence was remarkably high: 95.9% (163/170) tested positive for anti-HPV IgG and 90.0% (153/170) for anti-HPV IgM. Molecular analysis detected HPV-16 DNA in only 7.0% (7/100) of the subset, while HPV-18 was not detected. PCR-positive individuals had significantly higher IgM levels than PCR-negative individuals (p < 0.0001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the discrepancy between widespread seropositivity and low molecular detection as suggesting transient viremia linked to occupational exposure among healthcare workers. They highlighted this as a novel observation in this occupational cohort.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that serological screening alone may overestimate active HPV infection risk in healthcare workers, underscoring the need for molecular confirmation in surveillance and infection control programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used convenience sampling and excluded high-risk groups, limiting generalizability. Vaccination status was self-reported, introducing potential recall bias. The small number of PCR-positive cases constrained advanced statistical modeling, resulting in a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated seroprevalence of anti-HPV IgG and IgM antibodies and molecular detection of high-risk HPV DNA (HPV-16 and HPV-18) among 170 healthcare workers in Iraq. Serological assays revealed exceptionally high antibody prevalence (95.9% IgG, 90.0% IgM), yet conventional PCR detected HPV-16 DNA in only 7.0% of a seropositive subset, with no detection of HPV-18. PCR-positive individuals exhibited significantly higher IgM levels than PCR-negative individuals (p < 0.0001). The authors interpreted this discrepancy as indicative of transient viremia potentially associated with occupational exposure. The study’s convenience sampling, exclusion of high-risk groups, and self-reported vaccination status limit generalizability, while the small number of PCR-positive cases constrained advanced statistical analysis, yielding moderate-strength evidence.
